survivability._classes: LOW / MODERATE / MATERIAL / CRITICAL, by EVIDENCE loss rather than by inconvenience. A provider that is tedious to replace but holds no unique evidence is not critical; a provider that is easy to replace but holds the only copy of something is.

Supabase.failure_mode: Project deleted, account lost, or provider ceases.
Supabase.what_is_unique_here: THE 33 EXECUTED CONTRIBUTOR CONSENTS. Evidence Ledger E-001 to E-004 cite their source as 'Live DB, pilot_contacts source=contributor-confirm'. The Master Register states the strongest rights evidence in the estate is Level B structured consent records, of which 33 people hold one. Also: bench_labels, bench_outcomes, study_runs, findings_history.
Supabase.evidence_loss: NO EXPORT OF THE CONSENT ROWS EXISTS IN THE REPOSITORY. Searching for 'contributor-confirm' returns five documents, and EVERY ONE IS AN ANALYSIS DESCRIBING the rows, not the rows themselves. If the project were lost, the estate would retain secondary descriptions of its strongest primary evidence and would lose the primary evidence itself.
Supabase.backup_status: NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether platform backups are enabled for this project cannot be determined from the repository and was not inferred.
Supabase.migration_path: Postgres is portable; the schema is in supabase-ALL.sql. The DATA is the exposure, not the schema.
Supabase.why_not_fixed_here: The obvious remedy -- export the consent rows into the repository -- IS REJECTED. Those rows carry names, emails and organisations. Copying them into a git repository would create a permanent, widely-cloned copy of personal data to protect against a hypothetical, which is a worse privacy position than the one it cures and contradicts the data-minimisation architecture. A controlled export held OUTSIDE the repository, or verified platform backups, is the right shape. Recorded as X-12.

_key_person_added_2026_09_19: THE PROVIDER DIMENSION WAS DONE ON 2026-09-18 AND THE HUMAN ONE WAS NOT. `survivability` answers 'if this provider disappeared, what evidence is unrecoverable'. It does not answer 'if this PERSON were unavailable, what could not be done'. Both questions matter to a transaction and they have different answers. Classification is by WHAT A SECOND PERSON COULD ACTUALLY DO, not by whether a document exists: documentation that nobody has ever executed is a claim about transferability, not evidence of it. Recorded here rather than in a new register, because this register already holds the dependency dimension and a second source of truth is what section 8 of the operating architecture forbids.

key_person._classes: LOW = documentation alone suffices. MODERATE = a qualified person could do it from the repository. MATERIAL = requires an account, credential or judgement only the owner currently holds. CRITICAL = requires the owner AND no documented path exists for anyone else.

_bus_factor_evidence.meaning: A bus factor of 1 is a TRANSACTION CONDITION, not a defect. It is the normal shape of a single-founder estate. It is recorded because a buyer will compute it in five minutes and should not find it unstated.

_transfer_requirements._why: The ten MATERIAL dependencies cannot be eliminated from this repository: every one needs an account, a credential or a judgement that is the owner's to give. What CAN be removed is the discovery exercise. Without this list, standing up a second operator begins with working out what they need; with it, it is one owner action against a named set. NO CREDENTIAL VALUE APPEARS HERE AND NONE EVER WILL; these are the grants to make, not the secrets themselves. THE COUNT ROSE FROM SEVEN TO TEN when a guard derived each class from the row's own evidence and found three rows -- security controls, privacy controls and public representation -- classified MODERATE on evidence that named the production console, a live database operation and a Section 23 owner act. Each is now recorded with its repository half, which does transfer, and its owner half, which does not.

not_transferable_by_a_grant.why: An attestation is the account of the person who was there. A successor can read them; nobody else can give them.
No Level A instrument exists, and Rule 8 forbids this repository determining title. Counsel, not a grant.
Reviewer consent is revocable at will and the relationships are personal. Recorded as a transaction condition, not a defect.
